clue.text: Key player, we hear

parts.note: a player of keys whom audiences go to hear performing live in a hall

explanation.surface: Someone important in a team is said to be pivotal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key player' suggests a star of a sports team; here the keys are those of a piano and 'we hear' is an audience listening at a recital.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: a soloist on the keyboard performing before a listening audience.

clue.text: Bar with standard action to oppose danger

parts.note: a bar in a pub or shop is a counter
a standard is a measure, a yardstick for judging

explanation.surface: A pub with a set routine for dealing with trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A safety step taken against a threat is the very sense of the compound noun, a synonym.

clue.text: State of bliss recalled in revised version's reminiscences

indicators.note: recalled read as called back, so the little word in is turned round

parts.note: RV is the abbreviation for the Revised Version of the Bible
ana is a collection of anecdotes or reminiscences about a person

explanation.surface: A blissful mood brought back by memories in an updated edition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns IN into NI. ANA, a crossword favourite, means a collection of sayings or memories of someone.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism the term names perfect peace and release, used loosely for any blissful condition, a synonym.

clue.text: Fragrant plant, though possibly inelegant

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of the next word may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A sweet-smelling flower that might nonetheless look clumsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges INELEGANT; 'though' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet briar, a wild rose with scented leaves, is a named example of a fragrant shrub.

clue.text: Beat easily, being right weight after initial training

indicators.note: after places the right weight behind the training letter in the answer
initial means only the opening letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: an ounce is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: An easy victory for someone at the right weight after early training, like a boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: To win by a wide margin over an opponent is a synonym for thrashing them.

clue.text: They're not, in fact, spineless about using AA

indicators.note: about here means turned around or rearranged, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Creatures that do have backbones, oddly said to involve the AA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges USING plus AA. The definition is fair because these lizards carry rows of spines along their backs.
explanation.definitionFit: These tropical lizards have a crest of spines along the back, so they are anything but lacking spines.

clue.text: Extraterritorial travellers left behind a sort of sound

indicators.note: behind puts the left letter after the space agency in the answer

parts.note: NASA, the US space agency, sends astronauts beyond Earth

explanation.surface: Space travellers leave a strange noise behind them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like a verb (departed); it gives L.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound made through the nose, as with m or n in speech, is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Shrink jeans, returning within a short time

indicators.note: within shows the short time is placed inside the turned jeans
returning means the brand of jeans is read backwards

parts.note: Levis are a well-known brand of jeans
hr is the short form of hour, a short time

explanation.surface: Jeans shrinking soon after being brought back to the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns the jeans brand round to SIVEL; 'within' then puts the short hour inside it. 'Shrink' is the definition, not an instruction to the jeans.
explanation.definitionFit: To wither and contract into a smaller wrinkled form is a synonym of shrinking.

clue.text: Understands what the addressee eventually does

definitions.meaning: to catch on, to grasp what someone means
literally, the person a letter is addressed to ends up receiving what was sent

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to grasp a hint, while literally describing a recipient receiving a communication.

clue.text: Stream in university to produce a painter?

indicators.note: in shows the stream is placed inside the other letters

parts.note: taken as written
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: A creek running through a campus, somehow yielding an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the stream inside the university letter plus 'to'. Maurice Utrillo was a French painter of Paris street scenes; the question mark flags the name as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Maurice Utrillo, the French artist famed for Montmartre scenes, is an example of a painter.

clue.text: A swell leader of panache in the American press

indicators.note: in shows the leading letter goes inside the other letters

parts.note: US is short for the United States, so American

indicators.note: leader of means only the opening letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: to press is to urge

explanation.surface: A dashing fellow heading the US newspapers with style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A swell' looks like a toff, but it is a rising, as in a swell of the sea; 'in' puts the leading P inside the American press.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden rise or surge, as of the sea or of feeling, is a synonym for a swell.

clue.text: Mark 2

definitions.meaning: Mark ..., the American author of Huckleberry Finn
an old word for two, as in never the ... shall meet

explanation.definitionFit: The pen name of the American author Samuel Clemens, and an archaic word for the number two.

clue.text: Tom has these lines tangled with vine

indicators.note: tangled signals the letters are knotted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone called Tom owns lines twisted up with a climbing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like a man's name but is a tomcat, said to have this many chances at life; 'tangled' mixes LINES and VINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Folklore credits a cat, a tom being a male one, with this many lives.

clue.text: A row when going for century in break shows keenness

indicators.note: when going for means the new letters take the place of the century letter

parts.note: a recess is a break, as in school or parliament
C is the abbreviation for century, from Roman numerals
a din is a row, a loud noise

explanation.surface: A quarrel breaking out during a pause shows eagerness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when going for' swaps the C in RECESS for A + DIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Being prepared and eager to act is a synonym of keenness.

clue.text: Model Phyl's a slim lady

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so the letters are reshaped into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, including the s

explanation.surface: Phyl, a fashion model, is a slender woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like a catwalk job but is the anagram signal; the S of Phyl's counts as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: A sylph is a slender graceful woman, from the airy spirits of folklore, a synonym.

clue.text: Hard work by company is kept under one's hat

parts.note: sweat is hard toil
a band is a company or group of people

explanation.surface: Hard work by a firm is kept secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept under one's hat' looks like the idiom for secret, but here it is literal: the strip lining the inside of a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: The absorbent strip fitted inside the crown of a hat sits literally under the hat.

clue.text: Cut out first letter in language

indicators.note: in shows the first letter is put inside the language

parts.note: Erse is Scottish Gaelic, a language
A is the first letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Removing the opening letter from a language.
explanation.definitionFit: To delete or wipe out something written is a synonym of cutting it out.

clue.text: Bright colour, not a tan for a change

indicators.note: for a change signals the letters are altered into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A vivid shade that is not a suntan, just to be different.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' rearranges NOT A TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Annatto is an orange-red dye from a tropical seed, an example of a bright colouring.

clue.text: MEP? Use him to spread an inoffensive word

indicators.note: to spread means the letters are scattered and laid out anew

explanation.surface: A politician asks us to employ him to put about a polite term.
explanation.walkthrough: MEP is a Member of the European Parliament; 'to spread' rearranges MEP and USE HIM.
explanation.definitionFit: A euphemism is a mild word substituted for a harsh one, a synonym of inoffensive term.

clue.text: Do they wear "going away" clothes?

parts.note: a going-away outfit is worn by a bride leaving her wedding; here the couple are going away in secret to marry

explanation.definitionFit: Couples who run off secretly to wed are literally going away, hence the joke about their outfits.

clue.text: Plant me in top ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters are broken up and remixed

explanation.surface: Instruction to put me in the top soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like soil, but it is the past tense of grind; it rearranges ME IN TOP.
explanation.definitionFit: The pimento is a sweet pepper plant, also the allspice tree, so an example of a plant.

clue.text: Being arranged like a communication cord

definitions.meaning: the emergency cord passengers pull is fitted aboard a railway carriage

explanation.walkthrough: A communication cord is the British name for the emergency brake cord on a passenger train.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in progress or set up, and literally where an emergency cord is found: aboard a railway carriage.

clue.text: Desert one? It's a big blow

definitions.meaning: a storm of the desert, whipping up grains
a violent wind, a blow being a gale

explanation.definitionFit: A gale carrying clouds of grit is a storm typical of deserts, and a strong wind is a blow.

clue.text: Singer loses head to a second Spanish gentleman

indicators.note: loses head to means the opening letter is replaced by the following piece

parts.note: a tenor is a male singer
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A vocalist is beheaded by a Spanish man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses head to' swaps the T of TENOR for S.
explanation.definitionFit: Señor is the Spanish form of address for a man, the equivalent of sir or mister.

clue.text: Bears seen in a nameless Devon town

indicators.note: nameless says the name abbreviation is removed

parts.note: Totnes is a market town in Devon, a county in south-west England

explanation.surface: Bears spotted in an anonymous town in Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nameless' drops N, the abbreviation for name, from TOTNES.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote something is to carry it, and bears in the sense of carries is a synonym.

clue.text: A group of assistants to express regret about European money

indicators.note: about means the regret word goes around the other letters

parts.note: to rue is to regret
tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: Aides apologise about the cost in euros.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the regret word around the European money; tin is old British slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is a body of attendants following an important person, a synonym.

clue.text: River — a river once more flowing back

indicators.note: flowing back means the whole run of letters is read in reverse

parts.note: once more means again

explanation.surface: A river returns, flowing backwards again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowing back' turns A + R + AGAIN round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Niagara is the river joining Lake Erie to Lake Ontario, an example of a river.

clue.text: Writers, they say, are in agreement

indicators.note: they say signals that the word is to be heard rather than spelled

parts.note: correspondents are letter writers

explanation.surface: Authors, people claim, are of one mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they say' turns the word for letter writers into its sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: When things match or tally they correspond, so this noun means agreement or similarity.
